bridge_gaps_exposed: The bridge compares a null-genotype row against the null disease row (a sign comparison only); the wild-type and heterozygote rows differ in genotype and are therefore reported as not comparable. That non-comparability is the specificity failure, and no summary field expresses it: read the assertion notes.
The Ser9 disease row has no drug-side row: lithium's effect on Ser9 was not measured.

candidate.name: Lithium as a WWOX-specific disease modifier

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried, and none may be derived from this card.

directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED means no matched comparison exists, which is a statement about the record, not about the biology.
A genetic or tool-compound row is not a row for the named drug: the identity of what was given is written in each assertion.
label_lookup is NOT_ATTEMPTED on every card: the bridge has no network and no pharmacological-label search was run. It is not NO_MATCH_FOUND.
No dose, route, schedule or paediatric suitability appears; concentrations and vector quantities of the sources are deliberately not reproduced.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE at class level.

evidence_against: SPECIFICITY FAILED: lithium suppressed the provoked seizure in all three genotypes, wild type included (Figure 7d; entries 0, 22).

The causal attribution to GSK3beta rests on lithium alone; the paper's own Discussion names lithium's other documented actions, including Wnt/beta-catenin-dependent effects (entry 3). Lithium acts on many targets besides GSK3beta.

The only cell-line source (Wang 2012, PMID 22193544) reports Ser9 phosphorylation unchanged during retinoic-acid differentiation of SH-SY5Y cells, while WWOX rose (entry 5): that is a WWOX-gain, differentiation context, not a WWOX-loss measurement, and must not be read as a knockdown result; the knockdown experiment of that paper measured Tau phosphorylation (entry 8), not Ser9.
Direction conflict (INFERENZA): beta-catenin stabilisation by lithium would push an axis that is already raised in WWOX-loss organoids (map record R-04, axis M5; card P4-D-02).
Different control groups and schedules for lithium and ethosuximide inside one figure (entries 27, 28): the two drugs are not compared on equal terms.
A clinical anticonvulsant effect would be symptomatic: CLAIM 031 states that seizure control does not buy development.

mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Symptomatic seizure suppression in a provoked-seizure assay; not WWOX-specific (wild type responds). Not deep recovery; WWOX function would remain lost. Track B: no allele-specific datum.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was opened for this card. Every locator is an existing entry of the deep-dive manifests PMID32000863.json and PMID22193544.json; the figure statements are those entries' own.
not_known: Whether lithium does anything in a Wwox-deficient system that it does not do in a wild-type one (the one experiment that tested it answered no).
Whether lithium moves GSK3beta Ser9 phosphorylation or kinase activity in a Wwox-null brain: lithium's effect on the Ser9 readout was not measured in this system.

Whether GSK3beta abundance or Ser9 state tracks activity here: abundance and activity are dissociable in this very system (S9-independent inhibition), and no kinase-activity assay exists in a WWOX system.
Whether the null-genotype hypersusceptibility is a driver of the developmental phenotype or an amplifier on a malformed brain (entry 6).
Whether the wild-type response is floor-limited in a way that hides a genotype difference.
Any allele-specific datum (Q230P class or splice allele): none exists for lithium.
Net direction on the Wnt axis: lithium stabilises beta-catenin, and WWOX-loss organoids show nuclear beta-catenin already raised (card P4-D-02).

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (disease-models/wwox/research/drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven separate queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN beyond non-specific seizure suppression; direction on the Wnt axis possibly adverse (INFERENZA).
p4_card.identity: Lithium (the salt used in the mouse experiment: lithium chloride; the clinical compound class is lithium carbonate), used in the one WWOX experiment as a tool inhibitor of GSK3beta. Map records R-04 (repurposing) and N-02 (negative translation) describe the same candidate and are linked to this one card.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Symptomatic seizure suppression is the only endpoint ever tested in a WWOX system; it is non-specific (wild type responds equally). A WWOX-specific disease-modifying rationale is not supported by the primary data. Transfer to the reference genotype: not established.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: GSK3beta (among many); claimed: inhibits a kinase de-repressed by WWOX loss; the de-repression is read from a single Ser9 phosphorylation blot; the attribution of the seizure effect to GSK3beta rests on lithium alone.
p4_card.next_measurement: A provoked-seizure arm with an explicit, tested null versus wild-type contrast and the interaction reported, or a different GSK3beta inhibitor under the same design; and a kinase-activity or substrate-phosphorylation readout in a Wwox-null system. Until then no genotype-specific claim is available.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: Already studied once (Cheng 2020, one laboratory, one experiment). Not new; the question is whether the result means what it was read as meaning.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE; Track A (allele-blind); not deep recovery.
p4_card.pharmacology: Approved compound (class level, from map record R-04) with a narrow therapeutic index and monitoring needs; CNS exposure is not in doubt. Nothing here is a statement about exposure in WWOX-DEE.

scope_of_checks.card_inferences_owed_audit: The direction-conflict statement on the Wnt axis and the amplifier-not-driver reading are INFERENZA and are owed a blind audit by another actor.

scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: One laboratory, one experiment; no replication.

p4_card.status_reason: The one experiment failed its specificity test and the Wnt-axis direction may be adverse.
p4_card.value_added: Keeps the lithium result as what it is (non-specific symptomatic suppression, specificity failed) so it is not read as a WWOX-specific signal, and names the contrast that would change that.

input.axis: E / Lucas-Clarke follow-up: pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase
bridge_gaps_exposed: The fly row has direction UNKNOWN by design: the study did not measure this branch, so no comparison is formed.
card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried.
directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED is a statement about the record, not about the biology.
Every disease-side row from the Drosophila article is NOT WWOX-DEE EVIDENCE; the organoid rows are exploratory transcript analyses of one deposit.
Abstract-level statements from PubMed are labelled abstract_only; none carries a receipt.
label_lookup is NOT_ATTEMPTED in the bridge: the bridge has no network. The openFDA adapter was run separately and is recorded in lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/compounds_and_sources.md.
No dose, route, schedule or paediatric suitability appears; assay concentrations of the sources are deliberately not reproduced.

curated_candidate.name: PDK inhibition (dichloroacetate and research PDK inhibitors) as the pyruvate-oxidation branch, kept separate from what the study measured

context.cell_type: adult fly head or brain (whole head for metabolomics and RNA-seq)
context.developmental_stage: adult, day 14 for omics and Atf4 imaging
context.disease_id: Drosophila model of Alzheimer's amyloid pathology (not WWOX-DEE)
context.genotype: neuronal Wwox RNAi plus neuronal Abeta42 (Arctic) versus control RNAi plus Abeta42

disease_assertions.endpoint: any measurement
disease_assertions.locator: disease-models/wwox/research/deepdive_manifests/PMID42909904.json verbatim_locators.entries[44], [49]; dossier section 3 (pyruvate not reported; Fig 5D draws a TCA node with no data attached)
disease_assertions.measured_result_note: The study measured no pyruvate, PDH, PDK, flux, oxygen consumption or NAD/NADH. Whether pyruvate was tested is unknown; the MetaboLights deposit is not publicly retrievable (mtbls12344.md). Pdk, Pdha, Pdhb are absent from the significant gene lists, which is not a test. The paper's own heading and abstract speak of pyruvate metabolism, but that rests on transcript pathway over-representation (KEGG, including Ldh itself; Pepck2, CG11052 and Adh lower), not on a pyruvate, PDH or PDK measurement.
disease_assertions.source: PAPER 567 (published Lucas-Clarke 2026 article; Drosophila Alzheimer's-amyloid model; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: a fly amyloid model, not WWOX-DEE)
disease_assertions.target_id: fly PDH, PDK, pyruvate or pyruvate-to-TCA flux

context.disease_id: WWOX-deficient human cerebral organoid model (engineered knockout; NOT a patient allele; no amyloid)
context.genotype: WWOX knockout versus wild type (4 versus 2 libraries, one laboratory)

disease_assertions.endpoint: log2 shift, knockout minus wild type
disease_assertions.measured_result_note: PDK1 -0.34; the PDK/PDH set +0.17 (P 0.22, not different from chance); LDH-to-PDH ratio not shifted (inside the spread of the two wild-type libraries). EXPLORATORY NEGATIVES: transcripts are not PDH activity, flux or metabolite, and do not show that PDH or lactate are normal.
disease_assertions.source: GSE156243, the deposit of the 2021 organoid paper (PMID 34268881); exploratory set-level analysis by scientist-c
disease_assertions.target_id: human PDK1 transcript and the PDK/PDH transcript set

context.disease_id: WWOX-deficient human cerebral organoid model (engineered knockout; NOT a patient allele; no amyloid)
context.genotype: WWOX knockout versus wild type (4 versus 2 libraries, one laboratory)

disease_assertions.endpoint: log2 shift, knockout minus wild type
disease_assertions.measured_result_note: LDHA +0.75 by the script's shift (+0.91 on the authors' list, padj 5e-6). LDHA also falls with elapsed culture time in WWOX-unperturbed spheroids, so the rise is as consistent with a less advanced tissue as with a WWOX effect. Transcript, not activity.
disease_assertions.source: GSE156243, the deposit of the 2021 organoid paper (PMID 34268881); exploratory set-level analysis by scientist-c

context.disease_id: enzyme assays and a congenital lactic acidosis indication (not WWOX)

drug_assertions.endpoint: pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase inhibition by dichloroacetate
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Curated PDK inhibitor. In the measurements retrieved the enzyme assay shows no half-maximal inhibition at the highest concentration tested and a fibroblast lactate-oxidation effect appears at a high micromolar concentration: weak in vitro. The repository's existing safety position (peripheral neuropathy, BLOCK-1) is unchanged by this card.
drug_assertions.source: ChEMBL curated mechanism and activity rows of CHEMBL306823; Open Targets (phase 3, congenital lactic acidosis); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: PDK activity (family target; rat enzyme assay) and lactate oxidation in human fibroblasts

context.disease_id: enzyme assay, not a disease

drug_assertions.endpoint: PDK2 inhibition by AZD7545 or VER-246608
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Research tool compounds; no CNS, paediatric or clinical datum retrieved. The symbol PDK1 in DGIdb returns PDPK1 agents (collision documented in target_resolution.tsv); only PDK2-4 rows and UniProt-keyed ChEMBL rows are used.
drug_assertions.source: DGIdb (Drug Repurposing Hub, Guide to Pharmacology) and ChEMBL activity rows of CHEMBL3392645; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE

mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: A bypass of a postulated bottleneck: partial benefit at best, and only if the bottleneck exists. Not deep recovery. Track B: none.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was newly read in full for these cards. The Lucas-Clarke reading is scientist-a's (receipt FTR-20261026-42909904-01); the compound statements are abstract-level PubMed reads and registry-database retrievals (lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/).
not_known: Whether PDH activity or pyruvate oxidation is altered in any WWOX-deficient human neural system.
Whether pyruvate was tested in the fly metabolomics (MTBLS12344 not publicly retrievable).
Whether the Ldh rise diverts pyruvate from oxidation at all.

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

against: The study measured nothing in this branch.
PDK1 transcript is down and the PDK/PDH set is not different from chance in the human knockout organoid (exploratory transcripts).
The sima:GFP reporter (the authors' HIF1alpha homologue) is unchanged in one genotype pair; the authors name Atf4 rather than sima as primarily responsible.
Known neurotoxicity concern for the main compound; the ketogenic hypothesis dominates it on safety.
for: The Lucas-Clarke Ldh rise is the kind of change that could draw pyruvate away from oxidation (logic only).
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: No datum from any WWOX system at the activity or flux level.

p4_card.identity: Dichloroacetate (PDK inhibitor, phase 3 per Open Targets for congenital lactic acidosis, no US label found) and research PDK inhibitors (AZD7545, VER-246608). Devimistat is NOT counted: DGIdb gives it no action type on PDK2-4.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF a pyruvate-oxidation block exists in WWOX-deficient neural cells. Nothing in the Lucas-Clarke study tests that; the branch logic (a raised Ldh pulls pyruvate away from oxidation) is indirect by two steps.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: PDK1-4 (HGNC:8809-8812; UniProt Q15118, Q15119, Q15120, Q16654), NOT PDPK1 (HGNC:8816); direction: release PDH from inhibitory phosphorylation; context: no WWOX system.
p4_card.next_measurement: The same discriminating assay as the ketogenic hypothesis, one step finer: PDH activity and labelled-glucose fate in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells. If PDH activity and pyruvate fate are normal, HYP-20260709-05 stays parked with a stronger negative; if pyruvate oxidation is blocked, this card and the ketogenic hypothesis are both reopened.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NOT NEW: HYP-20260709-05 and N-08 already hold this candidate (parked; dominated by the ketogenic hypothesis; peripheral-neuropathy flag).
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.
p4_card.pharmacology: Dichloroacetate: weak in the retrieved enzyme and cell assays; no label found; spontaneous-report counts exist but are not rates. Research PDK inhibitors: enzyme tools only.

scope_of_checks.card_inferences_owed_audit: Statements marked INFERENZA, including every statement about what a compound would do in WWOX-deficient tissue, are OWED a blind audit by another actor.
scope_of_checks.formal_checks: Disease-side fly rows carry verbatim locators in the manifest (104 entries; entries 31, 49, 89, 94 SUPPORTED by a blind audit, entry 95 narrowed after an OVERSHOOT finding); the compound statements are abstract-level and unaudited.
scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: No independent replication of any fly row is held; the organoid rows are one laboratory's deposit.

external_not_wwox_evidence: ChEMBL curated mechanism and activity rows for dichloroacetate

p4_card.state_of_known_roads: HYP-20260709-05, N-08, DL-MECH-020 (HIF1A to PDK to PDH chain).
p4_card.value_added: Keeps the pyruvate branch SEPARATE from what the paper measured and records that three exploratory transcript tests are negatives that do not show normal PDH or lactate.

cellular_context.cells_tissue_stage: none measured in WWOX-deficient human neurons at the activity level.
cellular_context.limits: The transcript negatives are exploratory and do not show PDH activity or lactate are normal; the HIF1A-to-PDK-to-PDH step is unmeasured in any WWOX-deficient human neural system.
cellular_context.target_expression: PDK isoforms are expressed in brain; the WWOX-dependent level is UNKNOWN.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked PDH readout that a PDK inhibitor moves: PDH activity (or PDHA1 serine phosphorylation) and pyruvate fate (labelled glucose into acetyl-CoA, citrate, lactate) in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells; only then a functional endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for WWOX at the activity level. The Lucas-Clarke study measured no pyruvate, PDH, PDK or flux. In the human knockout organoid PDK1 is DOWN, the PDK/PDH set is not different from chance and the LDH-to-PDH ratio is not shifted (transcripts).
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Fly study with no measurement in this branch; transcripts from one organoid deposit; compound statements are database rows.

p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF a pyruvate-oxidation block exists in WWOX-deficient neural cells. Nothing in the Lucas-Clarke study tests that; the branch logic (a raised Ldh pulls pyruvate away from oxidation) is indirect by two steps.

cellular_context.limits: The transcript negatives are exploratory and do not show PDH activity or lactate are normal; the HIF1A-to-PDK-to-PDH step is unmeasured in any WWOX-deficient human neural system.
cellular_context.target_expression: PDK isoforms are expressed in brain; the WWOX-dependent level is UNKNOWN.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked PDH readout that a PDK inhibitor moves: PDH activity (or PDHA1 serine phosphorylation) and pyruvate fate (labelled glucose into acetyl-CoA, citrate, lactate) in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells; only then a functional endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for WWOX at the activity level. The Lucas-Clarke study measured no pyruvate, PDH, PDK or flux. In the human knockout organoid PDK1 is DOWN, the PDK/PDH set is not different from chance and the LDH-to-PDH ratio is not shifted (transcripts).
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Fly study with no measurement in this branch; transcripts from one organoid deposit; compound statements are database rows.

mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (disease-models/wwox/research/drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven separate queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the only synonym-driven record is one observational natural-history registry. Carried with the census's own caution: "A missing hit does not prove that no study exists." It answers seven queries against one registry on one date; unregistered, differently worded, non-NLM or later-registered studies are not excluded.

against: Not independently replicated within the repository; the source's mouse-versus-human construct comparison is an intra-study control, and the human-organoid source was not tested here.

SURVIVAL IS A STEP IN THESE DATA, BUT A STEP AND A STEEP CONTINUUM ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE: the lower level postpones death and reaches extinction; two dose points cannot locate a threshold; the adjudication in CLAIM 011 reads the step as strengthened, not established.
Body weight is equal at the two levels at one age and the weight comparison is survivor-conditioned on the lower side: an equality between unequal denominators is not evidence of grading.
Myelination dose relation never quantified; gliosis result binary against wild type with no untreated-null comparator; SWD has no low-level arm.
No tumour surveillance of any kind in a pro-apoptotic tumour suppressor delivered irreversibly; no measured ceiling.
Treatment age window tested only at the earliest postnatal ages; later NOT_MEASURED.
Behaviour at 3 months has no untreated-null arm by construction and a text-versus-panel conflict, not adjudicated.
for: SWD to a level not distinguishable from wild type in the strongest causal design of the corpus (blinded; single vector level).
Durable survival to 300 days at the higher vector level, comparable to the wild-type arm (which itself lost about 29 percent).
Graded WWOX protein, glycaemia at one age and motor score.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Null versus missense or compound context; mouse absence-type SWD versus human convulsive repertoire.

p4_card.expected_contribution: Recovery of function by replacement (R-class demonstrated in the null mouse); nothing is stated for clinical benefit.
p4_card.identity: AAV9 carrying human WWOX cDNA under a neuronal promoter, with and without a post-transcriptional element; the promoter-comparison constructs are a different architecture. Whether any programme's clinical construct equals the mouse-study construct: UNKNOWN. Titre convention is undeclared by the source and no vector quantity is reproduced here.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WOREE (all genotypes carry some level of WWOX deficit) as target; origin: a constitutive-null mouse and human knockout and patient-derived organoids. Transfer to a Q230P-class missense or compound context is not established.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: WWOX gene dosage in neurons; type: replacement; direction: protein up; context: null mouse brain.
p4_card.next_measurement: An intermediate-level arm, defined as a fraction of the primary's higher level (never in absolute quantity), carried to 300 days with survival, weight, glycaemia, ECoG and quantified myelin in the same animals; and an independent replication. Either would change whether this is a threshold or a steep continuum.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: Already studied (two mouse papers, one laboratory). A gene-therapy programme for WOREE is recorded at grant level (census § 3); that is not a registered study.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.
p4_card.pharmacology: Not applicable in the small-molecule sense: biodistribution regionally uneven; potency, selectivity and CNS exposure of a human product: UNKNOWN. The absolute vector quantity is uncertain by exactly a factor of two in the source and no figure is reproduced.

cellular_context.limits: Residual partial function in a missense context is a reason to expect a DIFFERENT result, not a larger one; the expected level of rescue in the reference genotype does not follow from this study in either direction.

evidence_against: The tool compound is not memantine: competitive versus uncompetitive antagonism, a slice preparation versus a living brain, and no exposure relation.

The paper's own burst-frequency numbers disagree between the main text and its supplementary table (entries 23, 24); the heterozygote incidence is a sixth of the knockout's and is called similar (entries 0, 1).

The control arm of the synaptic analyses pools heterozygotes with wild type under a conditional rule the paper does not show for the pooled measures (CLAIM 021 caveat; entry 9); the incidence figures used here keep wild type separate.

The same figure's pannexin-1 blocker raised burst frequency about two and a half fold with no significance reported, which both text and Discussion call no effect (entry 2): a lesson that this paper's prose and panels disagree and the panel must be read.
Suppressing a network state is not correcting a developmental lesion (CLAIM 031).

mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Symptomatic control of a network state measured in slices; not deep recovery; developmental benefit not implied. Track B: no allele-specific datum.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was opened for this card. Locators are existing entries of the deep-dive manifest PMID34634460.json; the d-APV Results sentence is quoted from the article text in the declared artifact.
not_known: Whether memantine itself reduces the burst frequency, duration, amplitude or phase-amplitude coupling in any Wwox-deficient preparation (it has never been given to one).
Whether the d-APV dependence holds with a low-affinity uncompetitive blocker at exposures tolerated in a child, and with the parental or rescue line as the internal comparator.
Whether the burst is a driver of the developmental phenotype or a network state on top of it (CLAIM 031: symptomatic control does not buy development).
Whether chronic NMDA-receptor blockade in a developing brain is acceptable where WWOX loss already impairs activity-dependent maturation (class-level concern in map record R-02, unsourced here).
Whether the effect transfers from a neuron-specific deletion at postnatal days 13 to 17 in a slice to a human epileptic encephalopathy.
Human-genetics corroboration (GRIN2A, an NMDA-receptor subunit, among burst-suppression genes; DL-MECH-002) is carried as context only: it was not re-read for this card.

abstention_card.an_abstention_is_a_result: The roadmap states it; this card names what would end it.
abstention_card.missing_datum: A dose-by-timing series of Wnt/GSK3/CK1 modulation in a developing cortex with progenitor, layer-neuron and electrographic endpoints, in any WWOX system; and a measured activation step (reporter or nuclear/cytosolic beta-catenin). Never administered in any WWOX system as a Wnt-lowering or tankyrase-type agent, and never as a dose-by-timing series. Two partial exceptions are in the repository: the CK1-alpha-inhibiting multikinase compound of the D01 card was given to knockout organoids (attribution among Wnt, MYC and CDK ambiguous), and a GSK3 inhibitor was given acutely to Wwox-null mice before a convulsant challenge with a seizure endpoint and a measured GSK3 phospho-state in brain (PMID 32000863, repository reading, text re-inspected); neither measures the activation step by reporter or beta-catenin. The transcript direction in organoids is the only Wnt-output measurement.
abstention_card.search_record: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test (known-roads § 2.4c, 2026-10-20); R3 adjacent query on tankyrase inhibition with neuro and development returned 2 records, one read.

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried, and none may be derived from this card.

directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED means no matched comparison exists, which is a statement about the record, not about the biology.
NO_MATCH_FOUND is not 'does not exist'; NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA is not MAI_TENTATO.
label_lookup is NOT_ATTEMPTED on every card: the bridge has no network and no pharmacological-label search was run. It is not NO_MATCH_FOUND.
No dose, route, schedule or paediatric suitability appears; concentrations or exposures of the sources are deliberately not reproduced.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE at class level.

evidence_against: SPECIFICITY FAILED: lithium suppressed the provoked seizure in all three genotypes, wild type included (Figure 7d; entries 0, 22).

The causal attribution to GSK3beta rests on lithium alone; the paper's own Discussion names lithium's other documented actions, including Wnt/beta-catenin-dependent effects (entry 3). Lithium acts on many targets besides GSK3beta.

The only cell-line source (Wang 2012, PMID 22193544) reports Ser9 phosphorylation unchanged during retinoic-acid differentiation of SH-SY5Y cells, while WWOX rose (entry 5): that is a WWOX-gain, differentiation context, not a WWOX-loss measurement, and must not be read as a knockdown result; the knockdown experiment of that paper measured Tau phosphorylation (entry 8), not Ser9.
Direction conflict (INFERENZA): beta-catenin stabilisation by lithium would push an axis that is already raised in WWOX-loss organoids (map record R-04, axis M5; card P4-D-02).
Different control groups and schedules for lithium and ethosuximide inside one figure (entries 27, 28): the two drugs are not compared on equal terms.
A clinical anticonvulsant effect would be symptomatic: CLAIM 031 states that seizure control does not buy development.

mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: qualified by several curated cards: P4-E-04; EB-KD-01; Track is read only from the card(s) that state it - EB-KD-01 state(s) a route and no Track (written before Track was qualified)
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was newly read in full for these cards. The Lucas-Clarke reading is scientist-a's (receipt FTR-20261026-42909904-01); the compound statements are abstract-level PubMed reads and registry-database retrievals (lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/).
not_known: Whether a WWOX-deficient human neural cell has a measurable bioenergetic defect that a ketone substrate would bypass.
Whether lactate is raised, normal or low in WWOX-deficient human brain across ages and contexts.

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: The fly lactate result is conditional on amyloid and cannot be used for or against the Warburg direction in WWOX-null neurons.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN beyond the empirical seizure-control use.
p4_card.identity: Ketogenic diet (HYP-20260709-01, map record R-05) and, as a direction control only, MCT1 blockade (AZD3965 in DGIdb). No new compound.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: A decision for the treating clinical team, not for this system; this card only records the consequence of the Lucas-Clarke reading: no direct support and no refutation.
p4_card.next_measurement: Seahorse OCR/ECAR on donor-derived WWOX-deficient cells (or the existing knockout organoids), as already specified in HYP-20260709-01.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NOT NEW: existing hypothesis, updated with a consequence note on 2026-10-26.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.

scope_of_checks.card_inferences_owed_audit: Statements marked INFERENZA, including every statement about what a compound would do in WWOX-deficient tissue, are OWED a blind audit by another actor.
scope_of_checks.formal_checks: Disease-side fly rows carry verbatim locators in the manifest (104 entries; entries 31, 49, 89, 94 SUPPORTED by a blind audit, entry 95 narrowed after an OVERSHOOT finding); the compound statements are abstract-level and unaudited.
scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: No independent replication of any fly row is held; the organoid rows are one laboratory's deposit.

external_not_wwox_evidence: DGIdb SLC16A1 rows: AZD3965 (inhibitor), valproic acid and sodium butyrate (no action type)

p4_card.state_of_known_roads: HYP-20260709-01 (ranked, proposed-to-L9), R-05, DL-MECH-020, DL-BIO-008, DL-BIO-009.
p4_card.value_added: Records that this paper changes nothing for the ketogenic hypothesis and names the one measurement that still decides it.

cellular_context.limits: No metabolic readout of the lever exists in a WWOX-deficient human neural system; the lactate rows have opposite signs in the fly (with and without amyloid) and in one human MRS report.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: The existing minimal falsifier of HYP-20260709-01: Seahorse OCR/ECAR on donor-derived cells or the existing organoids; this card adds no new endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: The ketogenic diet in WWOX-DEE: tried in 3 patients in one cohort and continued in 1; a null-genotype report where it was suspended. The Lucas-Clarke study contains no diet, ketone, PDH or pyruvate arm.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: n of 3 and n of 1 clinical reports; fly lactate is amyloid-conditional.

p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: A decision for the treating clinical team, not for this system; this card only records the consequence of the Lucas-Clarke reading: no direct support and no refutation.

bridge_gaps_exposed: The bridge compares fly and organoid rows only where target, endpoint and context match; none match, so the directional summary is UNRESOLVED by construction.

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried.
directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED is a statement about the record, not about the biology.
Every disease-side row from the Drosophila article is NOT WWOX-DEE EVIDENCE; the organoid rows are exploratory transcript analyses of one deposit.
Abstract-level statements from PubMed are labelled abstract_only; none carries a receipt.
label_lookup is NOT_ATTEMPTED in the bridge: the bridge has no network. The openFDA adapter was run separately and is recorded in lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/compounds_and_sources.md.

context.cell_type: adult fly head or brain (whole head for metabolomics and RNA-seq)
context.developmental_stage: adult, day 14 for omics and Atf4 imaging
context.disease_id: Drosophila model of Alzheimer's amyloid pathology (not WWOX-DEE)
context.genotype: neuronal Wwox RNAi plus neuronal Abeta42 (Arctic) versus control RNAi plus Abeta42

disease_assertions.endpoint: Atf4 fluorescence intensity
disease_assertions.measured_result_note: About 1.0 to about 1.2-1.3 normalised, n 6 brains, one antibody, four small regions of interest, y axis not at zero. Correlational. Atf4 is never knocked down or activated in the paper; PERK and eIF2 alpha phosphorylation are not measured.
disease_assertions.source: PAPER 567 (published Lucas-Clarke 2026 article; Drosophila Alzheimer's-amyloid model; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: a fly amyloid model, not WWOX-DEE)

context.cell_type: adult fly head or brain (whole head for metabolomics and RNA-seq)
context.developmental_stage: adult, day 14 for omics and Atf4 imaging
context.disease_id: Drosophila model of Alzheimer's amyloid pathology (not WWOX-DEE)
context.genotype: neuronal Wwox RNAi versus control RNAi in a LacZ (no amyloid) background

disease_assertions.endpoint: Atf4 fluorescence intensity
disease_assertions.measured_result_note: No change without amyloid (t 0.0894, P 0.9305, n 6 brains). A measured null in a different contrast, not an unmeasured cell.
disease_assertions.source: PAPER 567 (published Lucas-Clarke 2026 article; Drosophila Alzheimer's-amyloid model; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: a fly amyloid model, not WWOX-DEE)

context.disease_id: WWOX-deficient human cerebral organoid model (engineered knockout; NOT a patient allele; no amyloid)
context.genotype: WWOX knockout versus wild type (4 versus 2 libraries, one laboratory)

disease_assertions.endpoint: set-level transcript shift, knockout minus wild type
disease_assertions.measured_result_note: Mean shift lower than 10,000 random same-size sets (P 0.0005); the gene-level direction of three genes had been seen before the sets were fixed; nine set tests across two analyses, none corrected for multiplicity; six libraries, genotype and composition confounded. Transcripts cannot see eIF2 alpha phosphorylation or ATF4 protein. EXPLORATORY NEGATIVE for the transcript signature without amyloid; not evidence that the ISR is normal.
disease_assertions.source: GSE156243, the deposit of the 2021 organoid paper (PMID 34268881); exploratory set-level analysis by scientist-c
disease_assertions.target_id: ATF4 / integrated-stress-response canonical target transcripts (12 genes, declared before the set test)

context.disease_id: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (not WWOX)
context.genotype: sporadic and familial ALS, not WWOX

drug_assertions.endpoint: ISR biomarker output under an eIF2B activator
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Target engagement shown for DNL343, a brain-penetrant eIF2B activator.
drug_assertions.source: Nat Commun 2025 phase 1b abstract, PMID 40825784; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: ISR biomarkers (blood cells and cerebrospinal fluid)

context.disease_id: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (not WWOX)
context.genotype: sporadic and familial ALS, not WWOX

drug_assertions.endpoint: disease rate ratio relative to placebo
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Ratio 1.04 (95 percent credible interval 0.83 to 1.32) over a 24-week placebo-controlled period: no benefit despite target engagement and proof of mechanism in the earlier phase. Adults with ALS; says nothing about a developmental encephalopathy.
drug_assertions.source: JAMA Netw Open 2026 randomised trial abstract, PMID 42771346; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: ALS functional rating and survival (joint model)

drug_assertions.endpoint: recognition memory under an eIF2B activator (2BAct)
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Better recognition memory and less microglial activation and tau; amyloid burden not reduced; p-eIF2 alpha lower. Mouse, adult, 23 days, one study.
drug_assertions.source: J Alzheimers Dis 2026 abstract, PMID 42179084; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: object-recognition memory, microglial activation, tau and amyloid burden

against: Without amyloid the fly Atf4 signal does not change.

A paediatric dataset for an ISR-attenuating drug exists in a different, eIF2B-driven disease.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Amyloid load is the context of the fly effect; WWOX-DEE has no stated amyloid load. Adult neurodegeneration trials do not transfer to a developmental encephalopathy.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. If the ISR were elevated and harmful, attenuation could protect function; if it is adaptive, attenuation could add harm. Neither is measured for WWOX.
p4_card.identity: ISR attenuators: eIF2B activators (ISRIB and its clinical-stage successors), PERK-arm inhibitors, and repurposed compounds that reverse eIF2 alpha-P-mediated translational repression; guanabenz as the paediatric-experience member. Full per-compound table: lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/compounds_and_sources.md section 2.1.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF a WWOX-dependent ISR elevation is shown in a human neural system. Today the transfer rests on a fly amyloid model; the one human knockout transcriptome does not show the signature. No Q230P or null-allele datum exists.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: eIF2B (five-subunit complex, EIF2B1-5, HGNC:3257-3261) or the PERK arm (EIF2AK3, HGNC:3255); direction: attenuate the ISR; context: amyloid-stressed fly neurons in the paper; UNKNOWN in WWOX-DEE.
p4_card.next_measurement: Stage 1 (decides everything after it): eIF2 alpha phosphorylation, ATF4 protein and ATF4-target transcripts in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells at matched maturity, with and without a defined proteotoxic challenge. If not elevated, park with the reopening condition below. Stage 2 (only if elevated): an eIF2B activator versus vehicle on that readout and on one functional endpoint. In the fly: an Atf4 loss-of-function arm with the Ldh and lactate readouts.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test: no source retrieved links an ISR modulator to WWOX deficiency; coverage is DGIdb, ChEMBL, Open Targets, PubTator 3 gene censuses and eight PubMed searches on 2026-10-26, and DGIdb, ChEMBL and Open Targets are themselves empty for the eIF2B activators. A zero is a statement about those queries.

p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE (partial benefit through a downstream lever); Track A (variant-independent), Track B conditional and unmeasured.
p4_card.pharmacology: Per compound in compounds_and_sources.md: no eIF2B activity in ChEMBL for ISRIB or fosigotifator; DGIdb and Open Targets empty for the eIF2B complex; PERK inhibitors have enzyme potency in ChEMBL.

drug_assertions.endpoint: cellular effect of stiripentol versus enzyme-level LDH inhibition
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Cell viability and extracellular acidification fall at tens of micromolar, but LDH activity in lysate falls significantly only at the highest, hundreds-of-micromolar concentrations, and oxygen consumption and complex I NADH oxidation are inhibited directly and immediately; the complex I paper reports no inhibition of malate dehydrogenase. Cellular effects of stiripentol are therefore not attributable to LDH alone on the available data (the 2026 glioblastoma paper itself reports 'at least a partial role' of LDH). In a mouse glioblastoma xenograft stiripentol prolonged survival (log-rank P 0.002; the dose is given differently in the Results and the Methods, which may describe different cohorts). Tumour models: no seizure, neurodevelopment or WWOX meaning.

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

against: The Ldh rescue lacks an Ldh-alone arm, a Wwox-mRNA check and a lactate readout, and the authors cite Ldh knockdown as detrimental in other fly amyloid models.
Without amyloid lactate falls nominally and Ldh does not change.

Stiripentol inhibits LDH only weakly in the single-concentration measurements held (none gives a fitted potency, and the one at the highest concentration is the lowest), and it has other targets, including direct inhibition of mitochondrial complex I, that act at lower concentrations; any benefit would not be attributable to LDH.
LDHA in the organoid is as consistent with immaturity as with WWOX loss.
Human lactate in WWOX deficiency is reported normal or extremely low.
for: Ldh RNAi improved climbing in the amyloid-plus-Wwox-reduction fly genotype (once).
Ldh transcript and lactate rise together in that genotype.

Stiripentol is an approved paediatric epilepsy drug with an LDH link published in epilepsy models (2015 report; abstract-level here) and an LDH-directed analogue series exists; nedosiran shows LDHA lowering is tolerated in humans in the liver.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: The fly effect needs amyloid; stiripentol's approved use depends on co-administration with another antiseizure drug and does not establish brain LDH engagement.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. A partial locomotor benefit was seen once in the fly with Ldh RNAi; no human or WWOX datum.
p4_card.identity: LDH-directed levers: stiripentol (approved for a paediatric developmental epilepsy; weak LDH inhibition in vitro), GSK2837808A and other research LDHA inhibitors, and the LDHA-directed oligonucleotide nedosiran (approved for primary hyperoxaluria, liver-directed). Per-compound table: compounds_and_sources.md section 2.2.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF lactate or LDH activity is shown to be a driver in a WWOX-deficient human neural system. The one fly precedent is amyloid-conditional; human lactate readouts in WWOX deficiency are normal or low in the cited sources (DL-BIO-008, DL-BIO-009).
p4_card.mechanism: Target: LDHA (HGNC:6535, P00338) and LDHB (HGNC:6541, P07195); direction: lower LDH activity or lactate production; context: amyloid-stressed fly head in the paper; UNKNOWN in WWOX-DEE. For stiripentol the LDH link is not the established basis of its antiseizure use.
p4_card.next_measurement: In the fly: lactate (enantiomer- or isotope-resolved) in the Ldh-RNAi double genotype, an Ldh-alone arm, and Wwox mRNA in the double line. In human neural cells: LDH activity and the lactate-to-pyruvate relationship in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic cells at matched maturity. Only then a compound arm: stiripentol against a selective LDHA tool at matched exposure, so that its other pharmacology is separable from LDH. The designed comparison (question, model, controls, endpoint, result that would change interpretation) is in sada_ldh_precedent_p2a_20261026.md section 6; it is a proposal, nothing is authorised to run.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test: no source retrieved links an LDH inhibitor to WWOX deficiency; coverage is the six sources of compounds_and_sources.md and ten PubMed abstracts on 2026-10-26. Update 2026-10-26 (scientist-b, P2a): the 2015 report usually cited for stiripentol and LDH in epilepsy (PMID 25792327) is now identified, is paywalled with no lawful full text found, and is known here only through its abstract and three open-access secondary descriptions; it is a stiripentol-LDH precedent in epilepsy models, not a WWOX datum.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: Stiripentol label: indicated for Dravet syndrome seizures in patients taking clobazam, from six months of age (openFDA label 2026-04-27); the same label means any use here would sit on top of clobazam co-therapy, an interaction this card does not assess. No paediatric suitability for WWOX-DEE is presumed.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE; Track A, Track B untested.
p4_card.pharmacology: Stiripentol: marketed formulation with a paediatric label for Dravet syndrome with clobazam; weak LDH inhibition in single-concentration enzyme measurements (no fitted potency; sizes differ between racemate, enantiomers and a database document), effective concentrations for LDH above total plasma levels and far above estimated free tissue levels in a review, other targets at lower concentrations; brain LDH engagement in vivo is asserted by secondary sources citing the 2015 report but not verified here. GSK2837808A: potent on LDHA in vitro, no in vivo or CNS datum retrieved. Nedosiran: liver-directed.
